summary: Outlines a continuous deployment workflow: automated dev VMs, CI (such as Jenkins) deploying to staging on every change with pass/fail tests, then the same playbook against production; requires a culture of automated QA.
questions: Can I use Ansible for continuous deployment?
How do I set up Jenkins to deploy with Ansible to staging then production?
What should I do if most of my QA is still manual?

answer_card.title: Continuous deployment with Ansible
answer_card.answer_md:
Example workflow:

1. Automate deploying local development VMs.
2. A CI system like Jenkins deploys to staging on every code change.
3. The deploy job runs test scripts to pass or fail the build.
4. On success, run the same playbook against production inventory.

Some teams deploy many times an hour this way, but it needs strong automated QA. With mostly manual QA, still use rolling updates and basic checks with `script`, `stat`, `uri` and `assert`.
